David Walliams subject of sexual misconduct allegations

Tuesday 10th November 2026, 12:54pm

  • ITN News and The Guardian have published a report which includes multiple allegations that David Walliams preyed on teenage girls and young women for sexual purposes. ITN has also published an hour-long documentary via YouTube
  • One woman in the report described her encounter with Walliams at 15 years-old as a "sexual assault"
  • Walliams denies all allegations against him, stating: "I am not a sexual predator... I have not broken the law"
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:56
Instaread

A three-year joint investigation by ITN News and The Guardian published today has revealed multiple allegations that David Walliams preyed on teenage girls and young women for sexual purposes.

Walliams had previously attempted to block the media outlets from publishing the allegations via a court injunction, however this was rejected by a judge on 3rd November.

Investigative journalists interviewed multiple women who encountered Walliams to build their report, with several of them accusing Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers. One woman in the report described her encounter with Walliams at 15 years-old as a "sexual assault".

Guardian reporters Maeve McClenaghan and Rachael Healy write: "Multiple women allege Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were teenagers or young women."

The stories reported include a woman who, at age 15, met Walliams, then 32, at a fan event. They kept in touch and, by the age of 17, they were having sex. The woman alleges Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on her for sexual purposes, saying: "I think I was groomed, 100%. We met when I was 15 and he was promising to help me and was a figure of authority and someone that I looked to for guidance and help. He used that power and abused that power the minute he felt he just about could and it was just about safe to."

The media outlets also accuse the Little Britain star of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment on the set of Britain's Got Talent and at HarperCollins, the publisher of his children's books.

Walliams, who is now 55, denies any wrongdoing. In a letter addressed to the journalists working on the investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."

He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."

The full report, which includes examples of messages Walliams sent young women and their accounts of what happened next, can be read via The Guardian

    How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

    CMP privacy choices

    Storage, duration, and usage details

    The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
    • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
    • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
    • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
